name: history
description: Shows previously executed commands; combined with ! expansion it re-runs them.

flags.description: Re-run the previous command (often as sudo !!).
Re-run the most recent command starting with "string".
Interactive reverse search: type a fragment, press Ctrl+R again to cycle.

examples.output:
998  systemctl status nginx
  999  journalctl -u nginx
 1000  sudo nginx -t
examples.explanation: Your last five commands with their numbers.
Reverse-searches history interactively — the single most useful shell shortcut once learned.
Environment variable controlling how many commands bash remembers (set it in ~/.bashrc).

about: bash saves history in ~/.bash_history on exit. Useful settings: HISTSIZE/HISTFILESIZE (length), HISTCONTROL=ignoredups:erasedups, and HISTTIMEFORMAT="%F %T " to timestamp entries. Ctrl+R search and Alt+. (paste last argument) dramatically speed up terminal work.
useCases: Recover a long command you typed earlier.
Re-run complex commands with one keystroke.
Document what was done on a server.
mistakes: Believing history is private — it is a plain file readable by anything running as your user.
warnings: Secrets typed on command lines are stored in history forever. Prefix a command with a space to skip history (HISTCONTROL=ignorespace) or use read -s in scripts.
